column3: Outdated: the ruling (published 2008-10-01, Shards of Alara) gives as its example an Illusion token sharing the name of the split card Illusion // Reality. Since the Kaldheim rules update (the earliest ruling in the data stating it is Battle for Bretagard's, 2021-02-05), a token whose name the effect creating it doesn't specify is named after its subtypes plus the word "Token" (CR 111.4: "If the spell or ability doesn’t specify the name of the token, its name is the same as its subtype(s) plus the word “Token.”"), so an Illusion token is named "Illusion Token" and Clarion Ultimatum finds no Illusion // Reality for it. Only this example is outdated: the rest of the ruling (a nonpermanent card found stays in the library) is cited in tests/rulings/r_p191_resolution.rs (clarion_ultimatum_only_finds_permanent_cards). See docs/RULING_DISCREPANCIES.md.
